description: This donut chart, titled “Stimulus Type,” visually represents the distribution of various input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs during WildChat conversations, with each category labeled and color-coded. The chart is divided into nine distinct slices, each corresponding to a specific stimulus type and its percentage share of the total. The largest segment is “Draft/Other” at 26.4%, shown in a dark red hue. Following this are “Press Release” at 18.7% (yellow), “External News Article” at 18.1% (dark green), and “Interview” at 8.8% (dark purple). Other categories include “Organizational Report” at 7.7% (light purple), “Event Posting” at 6.6% (brown), “Organizational Website” at 4.9% (dark blue), “Intra-agency news article” at 4.9% (light blue), and “Email” at 2.7% (light green), with “Social Media Post” at 1.1% (orange) being the smallest. All percentage values are explicitly labeled outside their respective segments, and the chart features a central white space with the title “Stimulus Type.” The segments are arranged in a clockwise order from the top, generally descending in size from largest to smallest, though not perfectly sorted.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of various input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs during WildChat conversations, matched to online articles from two identified news agencies. The largest category is 'Draft/Other,' accounting for approximately 26.4% of the total, followed by 'Press Release' at 18.7%. 'External News Article' and 'Interview' are the next largest categories, representing 18.1% and 8.8%, respectively. Notably, 'Organizational Report' consistently exceeds 'Event Posting,' with 9.7% compared to 6.6%. Additionally, 'Social Media Post' shows a slight increase over 'Email,' with 1.5% versus 2.7%. The chart provides a clear overview of the relative proportions of each stimulus type, with all categories labeled and color-coded for clarity.
